original_question: Which phospholipid is overproduced in Lenz–Majewski syndrome, a condition caused by an overactive phosphatidylserine synthase 1?

final_qi.question: Which phospholipid is overproduced in Lenz–Majewski syndrome, a condition caused by an overactive phosphatidylserine synthase 1?
final_qi.search_keyword: Lenz Majewski syndrome phospholipid overproduced phosphatidylserine synthase 1
final_qi.long_answer: Lenz–Majewski syndrome is caused by gain-of-function mutations in the PTDSS1 gene, which encodes phosphatidylserine synthase 1. These mutations lead to an increased activity of the enzyme, resulting in the overproduction of phosphatidylserine, a key phospholipid in cell membranes.
